questiontext.text:
Select the pair of terms that represent different types of variables

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

The correct answer is Discrete and continuous.

These terms refer to types of variables. Discrete variables have distinct, separate values, often counted in whole numbers, while continuous variables can take any value within a range and are often measured with real numbers.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

The correct answer is Qualitative and Quantitative variables.

Qualitative variables, also known as categorical variables, are variables that represent categories, labels, or attributes. These categories are often non-numeric and describe different characteristics or qualities of items or individuals in a dataset.

Quantitative variables, also known as numeric variables, represent measurable quantities or numerical values. These variables are inherently numeric and can be subjected to mathematical operations, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

[[/ if ]]
